dataset.title: Speech steganography based on scrambling and hiding (Spanish audios)

described_contents.source_domain: Female speech recordings, as described by the dataset page.
described_contents.method: Scrambling and hiding; each secret is embedded in each host with six BH (bits-to-hold) settings.

relevance.positive: Independent audio steganography samples using a method different from the Sleepy Alarm ASK carrier.
relevance.benign: Original host signals are candidate benign references.
relevance.limitation: Not ASK 8 kHz; detector features specific to Sleepy Alarm may not transfer. Dataset description indicates a narrow Spanish-speech source.

proposed_split.unit: disjoint host_source_id AND secret_source_id groups; keep all six BH variants of each host-secret pair in the same split
proposed_split.rationale: Separating only hosts would still allow a secret recording to appear in both train and test; both source axes must be disjoint to reduce source leakage.
proposed_split.caveat: Only 10 host and 10 secret recordings are described; the source domain is narrow female speech. Validation/test sets are very small and results would remain exploratory.

note: Dataset discovery is not equivalent to collected/verified independent data. No archive has been downloaded, so no per-file manifest records or hash values are invented. Do not report metrics until archives are downloaded, license and integrity rechecked, sample records extracted and a source-disjoint split is frozen.

test_cases: same SHA-256 appears in multiple splits
validation_implementation.note: Unit-test fixtures validate checker logic only; no external corpus samples have been downloaded or checked.
